# Root substantive assent: runtime40/source430

Actual Claude Opus5 completed the independent review in Herdr wH:p6. I read the full REVIEW.md and structured report plus original hash list. Subject SHA-256 b4046feb32fde212812b7557d10898f8aa8b8a4a5febaf4cb846093ef1b1d168; review.json SHA-256 eaea5b721ac165646ac8f3b5621468846a77eaf3e95e7c77b864650305f53e02. ACCEPT-DESIGN-UNIT with no required findings is appropriate for the exact frozen standalone reader. Guarded activation verifies all original reviewer hash rows before preserving them and all formal/source pins before materialization.

The public wrappers bind a private charging algorithm to the original guarded scope/allowance. Bounds prevent arithmetic overflow; requested buffer growth and every read attempt are charged before execution. EOF returns the accumulated bytes; errors yield no prefix. Completeness here is relative to the Read implementation's EOF indication, not independently proven underlying-file completeness or stability. Private arbitrary-reader behavior remains outside the claim. Original IO error values remain intact. Allocator errors reported through try_reserve_exact become Reserve; this is not a guarantee against every allocator abort/panic or process failure.

I agree with the independent23 replayed tests (8reader/7ledgerintegration/6unit/2doc), clean workspace check and nine probe groups. Exact reserved allowance and Interrupted probes independently corroborate the numeric cost semantics. The initial reviewer assert_eq!/PartialEq probe mistake is explicitly acknowledged as harness-only; final corrected probe supplies the evidence. No full security suite or native custody qualification is inferred.

I retain fail-closed InvalidLimit semantics. The non-blocking suggestion to validate outside the guard is not adopted: a caller must not silently resume a shared operation after a helper refusal. Cumulative requested growth is not measured peak memory; the roughly12.6MB worst-case requested total does not establish allocator/RSS bounds. The growth-turn edge is the read-attempt edge, not a separately metered allocation API call.

The latching-before-return warning belongs in the source documentation as suggested. I will add that clarification in the next separately frozen source unit rather than mutate430. Runtime40 itself leaves every native adapter unchanged; original native required-postcheck composition remains open under audit429. Advice429 and private432/433/434/436 are not approved by this review. No actor/core/profile/custody/creator/P0/currentauthority or whole-M2/M2–M6 completion claim follows. Subject/formal/live checks and exact three-path materialization remain required before integration.
